title: Organoid Sample Preparation and Extraction for LC-MS Peptidomics
author: Miedzybrodzka, Foreman, et al.
materials: This step describes sample data acquisition of extracted samples by LC-MS analysis. Extracts are analyzed using a Thermo Fisher Scientific Ultimate 3000 nano LC system coupled to a Q Exactive Plus Orbitrap mass spectrometer according to the analytical parameters stated previously in LC-MS system set up.60.Prior to injection onto the liquid chromatography (LC) system, centrifuge samples at 3,500 × g for 10 min.61.Inject samples onto LC-MS system for analysis; recommended volumes of 30 μL for secretion supernatants and lysed organoids, and 40 μL for sorted cells.Note: See Troubleshooting 3 if chromatography is not as expected

steps.title: Extract peptides from lysed organoids
steps.instruction: Defrost organoid lysates on ice, then precipitate with a 1:5 volume ratio of 80 % acetonitrile (ACN) in water (transfer to a larger Eppendorf tube if needed). Centrifuge at 3,500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, collect the lower aqueous phase without disturbing the solid precipitate and transfer to a clean LoBind tube. Evaporate to dryness in a rotary evaporator (≈18 h, overnight). Re‑constitute in 250 µL 0.1 % formic acid (FA) in water (v/v) and load onto an Oasis HLB Prime μElution SPE plate, applying gentle positive pressure on the SPE manifold. Wash sequentially with 200 µL 0.1 % FA in water (v/v) then 200 µL 5 % methanol : 1 % acetic acid in water (v/v), ensuring plate reservoirs are clear. Elute peptides into a QuanRecovery plate with two 30 µL aliquots of 60 % methanol : 10 % acetic acid in water (v/v). Evaporate eluate under nitrogen at 40 °C on a Biotage SPE Dry 96 until dry. Re‑constitute in 75 µL 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, incubate 1 h at 60 °C. Add 20 µL 100 mM iodoacetamide in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, incubate 30 min at 18‑25 °C in the dark. Dilute with 25 µL 1 % FA in water (v/v). Note: Reduction and alkylation (steps above) can be omitted, but this reduces peptide identifications. For targeted quantitation, dilute the SPE extract with 75 µL 0.1 % FA after elution before LC‑MS/MS.

steps.title: Purify cell populations by FACS
steps.instruction: Recover organoids from matrix domes by aspirating culture media, adding 2 mL ice‑cold Advanced DMEM/F12 per 6‑well, scraping with a P1000 and collecting into 15 mL tubes. Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant. Digest organoids: resuspend pellet in 5 mL TrypLE Express per 6‑well, incubate 37 °C for 20 min, then mechanically triturate 10‑20 times with P1000 and P200 pipettes; inspect a ~20 µL drop under a microscope. Repeat incubation and trituration at 5‑20 min intervals until a largely single‑cell suspension is achieved (typically 30‑60 min total). Optional: transfer to a 50 mL tube during digestion to prevent settling, then return to 15 mL tubes for centrifugation. Small clusters of up to ten cells are acceptable. Wash cells with FACS media: centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, triturate 10‑20 times with P200 and P20 pipettes, resuspend in 5 mL FACS media; repeat this wash two more times and pass the suspension through a 50 µm cell strainer. Resuspend again in FACS media containing live‑cell dyes (e.g., 5 µM DRAQ5 and/or 2 µg/mL DAPI). Transfer the single‑cell suspension to 5 mL round‑bottom polypropylene FACS tubes and sort desired populations directly into 350 µL 6 M guanidine hydrochloride in LoBind 1.5 mL tubes. Aim for >10 000 cells per population (peptidomics works down to ~100 cells).

steps.title: Vortex and snap‑freeze sorted cells
steps.instruction: Vortex the sorted‑cell suspension briefly, then snap‑freeze immediately on dry ice. Samples may be stored at –70 °C until peptide extraction. Note: 10 % FBS in the FACS media introduces bovine peptides; for proteomics use 0.1 % BSA or lower FBS concentration.

steps.title: Extract peptides from FACS‑sorted cells
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen sorted‑cell samples on ice, refreeze on dry ice (or at –70 °C) and thaw again on ice. Add 900 µL 80 % ACN in water, vortex to mix. Centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, transfer the lower aqueous phase to a clean LoBind tube. Evaporate to dryness in a rotary evaporator (~18 h, overnight). Re‑constitute in 500 µL 0.1 % FA in water (v/v) and load onto an Oasis HLB Prime μElution SPE plate, applying gentle positive pressure. Wash with 200 µL 0.1 % FA in water then 200 µL 5 % methanol : 1 % acetic acid in water (v/v), ensuring reservoirs are clear. Elute into a QuanRecovery plate with two 30 µL aliquots of 60 % methanol : 10 % acetic acid in water (v/v). Evaporate eluate under nitrogen at 40 °C on a Biotage SPE Dry 96 until dry. Re‑constitute in 75 µL 10 mM DTT in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, incubate 1 h at 60 °C. Add 20 µL 100 mM iodoacetamide in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, incubate 30 min at 18‑25 °C in the dark. Dilute with 25 µL 1 % FA in water (v/v).

steps.title: Extract peptides from secretion samples
steps.instruction: Thaw secretion supernatants on ice. Add 50 µL 1 % FA in water (v/v) to each sample and mix gently (perform on wet ice). If performing targeted quantitation, add 50 µL internal‑standard solution prepared in 1 % FA instead of blank solvent. Transfer the mixture onto an Oasis HLB Prime μElution SPE plate and apply gentle positive pressure. Wash sequentially with 200 µL 0.1 % FA in water then 200 µL 5 % methanol : 1 % acetic acid in water (v/v), ensuring wells are clear. Elute into a QuanRecovery plate with two 30 µL aliquots of 60 % methanol : 10 % acetic acid in water (v/v). Dilute the eluate with 75 µL 0.1 % FA in water (v/v).

steps.title: Prepare samples for LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Centrifuge all peptide extracts at 3 500 × g for 10 min. Inject the cleared supernatants onto the LC‑MS system using the recommended volumes: 30 µL for secretion supernatants and lysed organoid extracts, 40 µL for FACS‑sorted cell extracts. Follow the instrument’s LC‑MS setup parameters as previously described; consult troubleshooting if chromatography is abnormal.

steps.title: Manually inspect peptide MS data
steps.instruction: Open the raw LC‑MS files and manually examine each peptide’s signature pattern, checking all observed charge states and the accompanying 13 C isotopic peaks to ensure accurate quantitation.

steps.title: Identify peptide m/z values
steps.instruction: Use Qual Browser (Xcalibur) to locate the m/z values of target peptides, then switch to Quan Browser (Xcalibur) to set up quantification, optimizing peak integration for each peptide’s retention time and charge state.

steps.title: Quantify peaks and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Export peak‑area values and compare them across samples using statistical software such as RStudio.
